messages:
sam: Heads up — seeing a tail-latency spike on SSE streams after the 1.12.0 rollout (started ~02:30 UTC). Likely related to tool-call heavy paths. Any observers? :eyes:
maya: I can repro on staging with a quick loop. Streaming stalls ~120-200ms between frames after the first chunk, looks like framing/coalescing delay rather than compute hotspot.
maya: Repro curl (staging):
```
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream -d '{ "model":"rw-otf", "prompt":"tokenize me" }'
```
maya: Quick log capture from staging (trimmed):
```
[streamer] frame_sent=0 t=0.000
[streamer] frame_sent=1 t=0.012
[streamer] frame_send_latency=0.182  <-- large stall between frames
[toolcall] serialize_ms=98
[protocol] sse_fragment_size=512 -> header-fragmentation
```
lee: Profiling snapshot shows `proto::serialize_header()` jumped from ~0.8ms to ~60-80ms on toolcall-heavy requests. Also seeing kernel-autoselect flip to fallback kernel more often because sequence length estimate changed slightly.
perf-bot: CI alert: perf gate failed for sse_stream_latency (p90 +38%) on canary. See run https://perf.redwood.ai/runs/98123.
toni: Did a quick bisect locally. Points to commit 4f9b2a1 (api/streaming: add header padding for client parity). Reverting that commit locally removes the inter-frame stall in my repro.
sam: Can you paste the bisect steps and exact commit hash?
toni: Bisect steps I used:
```
git bisect start HEAD v1.11.9
git bisect good v1.11.9
git bisect bad HEAD
# bisect pointed to 4f9b2a1 (api/streaming: pad sse headers)
```
lee: That PR added a 128-byte padding to SSE headers intending to align with some legacy clients. Side effect: packets are crossing our write-coalescing threshold and hitting a slower path in the router which increases per-frame latency. The PR also added an extra meta field in toolcall serialization which increases `serialize_ms`.
maya: Short-term mitigations I propose: 1) emergency revert of that padding change, 2) add runtime flag `sse.header_padding=0` (default 0 for now), 3) add microbenchmark for `proto::serialize_header()` into CI.
sam: Hold rollout (canary) until we have an action. @deploy-bot can you pause the canary? :pray:
deploy-bot: Canary pause/rollback initiated for v1.12.0 at 02:45 UTC. Staging + canary traffic frozen.
toni: Opening a revert PR now (will also add a compat opt-in header `X-SSE-compat: 1` for clients that need padding). Revert PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/api/pull/4432
lee: Also proposing a tiny runtime tweak: prefer primary kernels when sequence_length_variance < 8 to avoid unnecessary fallback kernel runs caused by the slight header-size variance. I can draft a PR for the runtime that adjusts the autoselect threshold and adds a unit test.
maya: I'll add the reproducible script to infra and a perf test which asserts `p95(sse_frame_interval)` doesn't regress >5%.
sam: Action items:
- toni: revert PR (urgent) -> link + perf run
- lee: kernel-autoselect tweak + unit tests
- maya: perf microbench + infra repro script
- sam: hold rollout, coordinate comms if customer impact increases
Thanks everyone. I'll update incidents page if we need to page. :thumbsup:
toni: Revert PR created and pushed. Running perf job now: `./dev/perf/run --canary api.streaming.sse_frame_interval`.
maya: Local perf run after revert: p95/p99 back to baseline on my canary cluster. Posting raw numbers to perf dashboard shortly.
sam: Good. When perf job is green we'll evaluate unholding canary. Keep updates in this thread.
lee: Note: follow-up work required to avoid reintroducing padding; we should implement the `X-SSE-compat` opt-in and document it in the API changelog.
perf-bot: Perf job 98145 finished: p95 back within 0.5% of baseline after revert. Canary hold recommended to be cleared after ops sign-off.
sam: Closing loop: toni, please merge revert + run canary perf. lee/maya prepare follow-ups. I'll clear the hold once ops confirm stable.
